newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani money rates close up in tight market.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani money rates close up in tight market.

text.p: Pakistani money rates closed up and overnight activity remained subdued amid a general lack of liquidity in the system on Tuesday, dealers said.
"The market opened with a bang with the news of the central bank raising the yield on its six-month security by 50 basis points," a KASB & Co dealer said.
A nominal amount of 53.3 million rupees was accepted at 14 percent at a weighted average of 13.64 percent.
"Pressure was on term repos as the one- and three-month tenors saw the most activity," the dealer said.

Banks were ready to pick up one-month funds at 16.5 percent but lenders were looking at 16.75. Three-month bids and offers were quoted at 15 and 15.50 percent but deals remained scarce, the dealer said.
Towards the end of the day term rates eased off marginally with one- and three-month offers quoted at 16.25 and 15.10 percent, but borrowers were hard to come by, he said.
"On Wednesday, the market will witness a net inflow of approximately one billion rupees by way of T-bills maturity and short-term federal bonds auction settlement," he said.
